question: A manager wants Claude to help draft a weekly customer newsletter, always drawing on the brand guide, the past issues and a fixed tone. What should the manager do first?
options: A) Paste the brand guide into a single long chat and keep returning to that same conversation each week.
B) Ask Claude for a first newsletter and add the brand guide only if the draft misses the intended tone.
C) Put the brand guide into the account-wide instructions so that it shapes every conversation they ever have.
D) Create a project for the newsletter work so the guide, the past issues and the tone rules sit together.
correct_answers: D) Create a project for the newsletter work so the guide, the past issues and the tone rules sit together.
explanations: One growing conversation is fragile and does not carry the direction into any new chat.
This defers the setup and produces a first draft with none of the context that matters.
Newsletter-specific material would then influence unrelated work across the whole account.
Correct. Recurring work with shared context and standing rules is exactly what a project is for.
